category.name: Properties of Matter
category.description: Density, pressure in fluids, atmospheric pressure, and buoyant forces.

lessons.name: Mass Density
lessons.description: Mass per unit volume of a substance, measuring compactness of matter.

worked_example.problem: An aluminum block has a mass of 540 kg and a volume of 0.2 m³. Calculate its density.

validation.error_message: Volume must be greater than zero.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Density is a characteristic physical property of pure materials. Water has a standard density of 1000 kg/m³ at 4°C.

lessons.name: Pressure
lessons.description: Normal force exerted per unit area of a surface.

variables.name: Pressure
variables.description: Normal force concentration (SI unit: Pascal Pa = N/m²)

variables.name: Contact Area
variables.description: Surface area of force application (SI unit: m²)

worked_example.problem: A force of 600 N acts perpendicularly on an area of 0.03 m². Find the pressure.

validation.error_message: Area must be greater than zero.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Smaller surface areas produce higher pressure for the same applied force (e.g. sharp needles vs broad heels).

lessons.name: Archimedes' Principle & Buoyancy
lessons.description: An object submerged in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of fluid displaced.

variables.name: Fluid Density
variables.description: Density of surrounding fluid (SI unit: kg/m³)

variables.name: Displaced Volume
variables.description: Volume of fluid displaced by body (SI unit: m³)

worked_example.problem: An object displaces 0.005 m³ of water (density 1000 kg/m³). Calculate the buoyant force.
steps: Given: V = 0.005 m³, ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²

sections.title: Flotation Principle
sections.content: An object floats when the upward buoyant force equals its total downward weight force.
